native_test_entries: test1: {'time': 1, 'state': {'rgb1': 'red', 'btn1': 'not pressed', 'btn2': 'not pressed', 'pot1': 0}, 'description': 'Initialization phase. After power-on or reset, the RGB LED should be red with default brightness (potentiometer at 0).'}

test2: {'time': 1.5, 'state': {'rgb1': 'off', 'btn1': 'pressed once', 'btn2': 'not pressed', 'pot1': 0}, 'description': 'First button interaction. After pressing btn1 once, the RGB LED turns off because it was in red (first mode) and btn2 was not pressed, but the test code expects off after btn1 press from initial red.'}

test3: {'time': 2, 'state': {'rgb1': 'blue', 'btn1': 'pressed twice', 'btn2': 'not pressed', 'pot1': 1}, 'description': 'Potentiometer and button interaction. The potentiometer is moved to position 1 (brightness adjusted), then btn1 is pressed again (second press), cycling from off to blue in the first mode sequence.'}

test4: {'time': 2.5, 'state': {'rgb1': 'red', 'btn1': 'pressed three times', 'btn2': 'not pressed', 'pot1': 1}, 'description': 'Button cycling. After pressing btn1 a third time, the RGB LED cycles from blue back to red in the first mode sequence.'}

test5: {'time': 3, 'state': {'rgb1': 'off', 'btn1': 'pressed three times', 'btn2': 'pressed once', 'pot1': 1}, 'description': 'Cross-mode interaction. With RGB LED in red (first mode), pressing btn2 turns the LED off as per the rule: if in first mode and btn2 is pressed, the LED turns off.'}
assumptions: Convert numeric test time to milliseconds; apply changed controls 400ms before observation unless explicit hold duration exists.
Normalized potentiometer positions0..1 map to ADC0..1023.
Every inferred button press is released after200ms unless an explicit hold duration is supplied.
Reference preflight required; no claim that reference consistency proves all prose requirements.
